items.summary: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA VS Babu, who represented Kolathur Assembly constituency, died due to cardiac arrest on November 19, , MGM Healthcare announced. He has been hospitalised for more than two months. As per the medical bulletin, the MLA had died at 2.24 pm . In a statement, the hospital management said: "Despite comprehensive medical management and the best efforts of our multidisciplinary clinical team, his condition continued to deteriorate. He subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest and passed away on November 19th, 2026, at 14:24 Hours." He joined the AIADMK in 2016 and later moved to TVK in February 2026, ahead of the Assembly election. BCI has advised students to ensure that the institution is legally authorised to impart the concerned law degree course and that the law degree satisfies the applicable requirements for recognition by the BCI for the purposes of enrolment as an advocate. items.title: Independent directors: A protective mechanism or a false sense of security?
items.summary: During a recent board meeting, a significant related party transaction was scrutinized and subsequently approved. Two years later, this transaction is now subject to investigation by regulatory authorities. Independent directors often perceive Section 149(12) of the Companies Act, 2013 as a safeguard against personal liability. As they are typically not involved in the management or daily operations of the company, this provision limits their liability to matters they were aware of through Board discussions that they either supported or contributed to or in cases where their due diligence was insufficient. However, the necessity for diligence fundamentally alters the interpretation of this provision; it necessitates tangible evidence of actions taken rather than merely serving an honorary capacity upon appointment. Defining what an “independent” director entails According to Section 149(6) of the Companies Act, 2013, a director qualifies as independent if they are neither managing nor nominee directors and if the board assesses them as honest with adequate experience and no ties to either the company or its promoters. A Bench comprising judicial member KR Saji Kumar and technical member Anil Raj Chellan held that the tribunal’s inherent powers cannot be exercised to permit withdrawal of liquidation proceedings in the absence of an express statutory provision. “The inherent power of the tribunal cannot be exercised to permit a withdrawal during the liquidation process, thereby conferring substantive rights on persons who would otherwise not be eligible to submit a resolution plan,” the bench held. PNB had initiated insolvency proceedings against OGD Services under Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). The NCLT admitted the company into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) in February 2023.
